A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title: the core activation, architecture and many experiments match. Both supplied documents are readable, including their figures, equations and tables. v3 includes Appendices A-C; v2 ends with references.

before.justification: v2 reports original image reconstruction, denoising, super-resolution, inpainting, occupancy reconstruction and architectural ablation results, although some baseline scores are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds modulation ablations, NeRF evaluation, DIV2K image representation and computational efficiency measurements, including appendix results.

M1.justification: BandRC's activation formula, complex normalization, prior conditioning and sigmoid parameter regularization remain in COSMO-RC. v3 adds a task-specific NeRF adaptation with eight complex layers, separate density and view-conditioned color outputs, and no prior embedder or positional encoding (Section 4.6). The principal method change is this adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 adds LEGO novel-view synthesis through NeRF, substantially extending task requirements beyond the earlier reconstruction tasks. It also adds DIV2K image representation in Appendix C.1 and replaces the Thai statue with Lucy for occupancy reconstruction. Kodak reconstruction, DIV2K denoising/super-resolution and Celtic-knot inpainting remain.

E2.justification: FINER, previously only cited, enters the reported Kodak, denoising, super-resolution, inpainting and occupancy comparisons. Comparator membership also changes within retained tasks: Gauss disappears from the Kodak image-20 comparison, and ReLU+PE disappears from denoising and occupancy comparisons. SIREN, WIRE and INCODE remain central comparators.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a NeRF protocol with 100 training and 200 test images, 400×400 training resolution and 200k steps, plus T4-based efficiency measurements and SSIM evaluation for super-resolution. Reported settings also change: v2's denoising learning/decay rates of 0.005/0.1 become v3's general 0.01/0.01, and the occupancy encoder description changes from truncation at layer 3 to its first five layers. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a modulation-on/off Kodak ablation (Figure 2), broadens coefficient analysis across activation parameters and functions (Figure 1), and adds computational efficiency analysis (Appendix C.4). v2's absolute spectral-error comparison in Section 3.3/Figure 4 is removed. The layer-frequency analysis and width/depth ablation are retained in Appendices B and C.3.

E5.justification: Figure 4(b) adds box-and-whisker summaries of PSNR variation across Kodak images, extending v2's means and individual-image plot with descriptive dispersion statistics. These describe variation across images, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither PDF reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds LEGO PSNR of 29.50 dB, DIV2K representation PSNR of 43.36 dB, FINER and super-resolution SSIM entries, and efficiency results. Thai-statue IOU of 0.992 is replaced by Lucy IOU of 0.995; these concern different objects. Shared Kodak mean PSNR of 41.24 dB and super-resolution PSNR values remain unchanged. The abstract's 6× margin changes from 1.03 to 0.64 dB, although both versions' tables imply 0.35 dB over SIREN: 27.66 versus 27.31.

T1.justification: v2 provides a brief polynomial/harmonic argument and coefficient comparison. v3 adds a general Fourier/convolution treatment and extensive Appendix A derivations concerning Chebyshev coefficient parity and complex modulation. The claimed argument that real and imaginary coefficients cannot vanish simultaneously substantially expands the theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion shift from introducing a raised-cosine activation that mitigates spectral bias to claiming a general structural limitation of symmetric activations and a rigorous complex-modulation remedy guaranteeing complete spectral support. COSMO-RC becomes an application of this broader theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: v3 emphasizes parity-induced spectral attenuation as the mechanism underlying performance, extending v2's bandwidth and coefficient-decay explanation. It newly states that the prior embedder can be replaced by extensive initialization search and explicitly discusses computational costs versus accuracy in Appendix C.4. Inpainting and occupancy advantages are also described more cautiously as marginal.

D1.justification: v3 supplies previously unspecified parameter bounds, T in [0,10] and zeta in [0,3], the prior MLP's (2,4) output shape, detailed NeRF implementation information and its code-base reference, and profiling hardware and FLOP-accounting scope. Conversely, v2's explicit ImageNet1K V1 pretraining, global average pooling and SiLU harmonizer details are no longer stated.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions the work around harmonic distortion and complex modulation. It newly acknowledges MIRE as including raised-cosine activations and cites Novello et al. on sinusoidal-network spectral behavior and stability. A dedicated harmonic-distortion discussion replaces the earlier prior-conditioning review, changing the relationship to existing research beyond citation updates.

P1.justification: v3 retitles and renames the work, substantially rewrites its abstract, introduction and conclusion, and presents spectral theory before activation design. Experimental descriptions are condensed, while the layer-frequency analysis and architectural ablation move into organized appendices. This is an extensive narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column presentation to a single-column conference layout. v3 redraws the architecture and coefficient displays, adds modulation, NeRF and Chebyshev-root figures, introduces a Kodak boxplot and efficiency table, and expands the super-resolution table with SSIM. It removes the frequency-response schematic and spectral-error figure and relocates several retained displays into appendices.

improvement.justification: The new modulation ablation, NeRF experiment, implementation details and measured computational costs improve validation and transparency. However, v3 makes guaranteed complete spectral support central, while Appendix A's parity derivation does not exclude other coefficient cancellations or establish that network-wide guarantee. New efficiency reporting also conflicts internally: Table 4 gives 38.7 forward GFLOPs where Appendix C.4 states 116. The empirical gains and stronger, insufficiently established theoretical claims leave the net quality direction uncertain.
